newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: $2.7 bln to flow into S.Africa equities in 97 - ING.
newsitem.headline: $2.7 bln to flow into S.Africa equities in 97 - ING.

text.p: Net new foreign inflows into the Johannesburg Stock Exchange are expected to soar to $2.7 billion in 1997 as emerging funds increase their exposure to South African equities, ING Barings said on Friday.
That compares to net inflows of $1.22 billion in 1996 and $1.34 billion in 1995.
Johannesburg-based economist Hania Farhan predicted foreign emerging market funds would increase their average weighting in South Africa to 6-7 percent by the end of 1997 from 4-5 percent at present.
This would still be well short of the weightings given to the country in the IFC Index, where it has 13 percent, and the BEMI Index, where it stands at 10.7 percent.
Farhan said new global flows into emerging markets in 1997 were likely to reach $50 billion, adding to the $260 billion current total of emerging markets money.
Six percent of that new money going to South Africa would yield $3 billion while an extra two percent weighting of total money would be worth $5.2 billion, making $8.2 billion in all.
However, some of that new money will be in the form of asset swaps between local and overseas institutions, in which case there will be no net gain for the JSE.
In 1996 assets swaps worth around 20 billion rand, or $4.7 billion, were concluded and in 1997 this should rise to 25-30 billion rand, or $5.5 billion.
Deducting $5.5 billion of asset swaps from the overall figure of $8.2 billion gives net new flows into the South African market of $2.7 billion in 1997.
